title: Network Reliability Theory Applied to Multi-Model AI Infrastructure

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: engineering reliability methods provide precise quantitative risk estimates. Fault tree analysis directly shows how correlated failures degrade system reliability compared to independent failures.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Reliability engineering mathematics (fault trees, common-cause failure models, reliability block diagrams) require specialized knowledge. CS beginners would need significant onboarding in reliability theory.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: derive analytical expressions for one architecture type, compute reliability as a function of correlation. Well-defined mathematical exercise.

novelty.reasoning: Web search found no published work applying fault tree analysis or reliability block diagrams specifically to multi-model AI infrastructure with correlated failure modeling. Fault tree analysis is actively used in traditional engineering and some AI explainability contexts (SCITEPRESS 2024), and there is work on using generative AI to facilitate FTA (ResearchGate 2024). However, the reverse direction — applying reliability engineering mathematics to quantify how correlated LLM failures degrade multi-model system reliability — is not addressed. The specific contribution of deriving analytical expressions for AI system reliability as a function of inter-model failure correlation is novel.

evidence: Machine Learning Models with Fault Tree Analysis for Explainable AI. SCITEPRESS 2024.
Facilitating Fault Tree Analysis with Generative AI. ResearchGate 2024.
